newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Lloyd deal offers growth prospect.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Lloyd deal offers growth prospect.

text.p: The proposed merger of insurance groups LLoyd Thompson and JIB will produce an international firm focused on profitable growth businesses, Lloyd Thompson chief executive Ken Carter said on Monday.
Carter, who will be chief executive of the 300-million-stg Jardine Lloyd Thompson Group Plc, told Reuters the impetus for the deal was the complementary nature of the firms' operations.

"The driver to the merger is not cost savings, it's entirely the business enhancements we can get out of the two groups coming together. The cost savings will be there but they would come out in the merger of any two companies," he said.
The merger, proposed on the basis of four New Lloyd Thompson shares for every five JIB shares held, is expected to be earnings-enhancing in its first year.

While Lloyd Thompson will contribute its experience and reputation, predominantly in London but also European and Bermudan markets, JIB, which operates in 30 countries worldwide, brings an international presence with a "very significant jewel in the crown" in Asia Pacific, Carter said.
He described the area as "one of the most exciting economic regions looking through the next twenty years".
He said the differences between the groups and the complementary nature of the operations were the prime motivations behind the deal.
The one area of duplication is in the London market, where cost savings will come in the administrative area rather than the front-end operations among brokers and business producers.
The newly merged group will be positioned between global brokers such as Sedgwick and Willis Corroon and smaller niche brokers such as Lowndes Lambert or C.E. Heath.

"We see Jardine fulfilling an essential demand from clients by being a very strong international broker focused on handling their business wherever it is in the world outside of the U.S., rather than looking to get a flag in every city in the world," Carter said.
Following the merger John Barton, currently chief executive of JIB, will become chairman of the new group which is to have its headquarters in London.

An extraordinary meeting of Lloyd Thompson shareholders will be held by the first week of February 1997 and the company is to pay a special dividend of 6.0 pence per Lloyd Thompson share, subject to the merger with JIB proceeding.
